assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of a scalar boson at the LHC completed the Standard Model and answered a question open for nearly fifty years. It is a clear, specific discovery, which is where I begin: the discovery first, then the people. The detector concepts and the 2012 analyses are original instrumentation and data-analysis achievements, and the significance is lasting.
assessment.attribution: The 2013 prize already recognised the theoretical prediction, so this entry concerns the experimental discovery. The credit is structurally collaborative. The founders and spokespersons of the two experiments are the defensible individuals: Jenni and Della Negra as the original ATLAS and CMS proposers, Gianotti as ATLAS spokesperson at the announcement. Virdee, the other CMS leader, is left out only because the limit is three, and that is an unresolved allocation.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation is complete: two experiments, many decay channels, and coupling and spin-parity measurements through Run 2. The interpretation is stable and the recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee will credit experimental leadership of very large collaborations over individuals is a policy question I cannot settle from the supplied text.
Which three of the four credited names best represent ATLAS and CMS is contestable; I have not independently verified the roles each person held in 2012.
Precision Higgs self-coupling and other properties remain open, though they do not affect the discovery claim.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Precision mapping of the cosmic microwave background anisotropies, including the acoustic peak structure, fixed the age, geometry and composition of the universe and underpins the standard cosmological model. As a cosmologist I regard it as one of the strongest discoveries in the field. COBE (2006) was the first anisotropy detection, but the acoustic-peak and precision-parameter era is a distinct achievement.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread across WMAP, balloon experiments, ground-based experiments and Planck. The WMAP leaders Bennett, Page and Spergel form a coherent configuration for the satellite-era precision mapping. Puget (Planck/HFI) and Sunyaev (theory of acoustic oscillations and the Sunyaev-Zeldovich effect) have strong claims that the three-name limit excludes. The balloon experiments that first resolved the first peak are not on the supplied list, so the allocation is genuinely unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature. WMAP, Planck, ACT and SPT agree to high precision, and the cosmological parameters have been stable for over a decade.
uncertainties: The supplied credit list omits balloon-experiment leaders who first resolved the acoustic peak; I am unsure how that bears on a fair prize.
Overlap with the 2006 COBE prize and with Peebles's 2019 cosmology prize may reduce the committee's appetite for a further CMB prize.
Persistent tensions such as the Hubble tension do not undercut the discovery but complicate the narrative.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube's detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, followed by the 2017 association with the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic-plane detection, opened neutrino astronomy at energies far beyond 2002's solar and supernova neutrinos. It is a discovery driven by an instrumentation concept, a cubic-kilometre detector in Antarctic ice.
assessment.attribution: Halzen was the intellectual driver of the IceCube and AMANDA concept, and Karle a principal figure in the ice detector's development and the neutrino analyses. A two-person credit is workable. The collaboration is large, and others, such as the AMANDA pioneers and the Baikal and DUMAND efforts, may have claims that I cannot assess from the supplied data.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is firmly established. Source identification is still partial: TXS 0506+056 is a roughly 3 sigma coincidence and NGC 1068 is about 4 sigma. The field is mature enough for the discovery claim but still developing in source physics.
uncertainties: The origin of the bulk of the diffuse flux is unresolved.
Recognition might be considered somewhat early before source populations are firmly identified.
I am not certain of the full history of the early detector concepts and cannot verify it from the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, delivers fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and enables relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and a possible redefinition of the second. This is a concrete, original invention with clear and lasting impact on metrology and fundamental physics.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed and first demonstrated the lattice clock concept. Ye's group drove it to the highest accuracy and stability and developed many-body clocks and frequency-comb links. A two-person prize is clean, with little ambiguity apart from other strontium and ytterbium contributors outside the list.
assessment.maturity: Mature: independent clocks worldwide confirm the performance and international comparisons are routine. The redefinition of the second is pending, so recognition is timely but a prize could also wait.
uncertainties: Hall and Haensch (2005) and Wineland (2012) already covered adjacent ground, so the committee may consider the area partially recognised.
Other contributors to lattice-clock development, for example in ytterbium, may deserve consideration; I cannot verify the relative priority from the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator by Kane and Mele, and its experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells by Molenkamp's group, is a clean theory-experiment pairing with a clear physical idea and wide consequences for topological matter.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele are decisive on the Z2 classification and the quantum spin Hall prediction. Molenkamp led the first experimental observation. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed HgTe, and Zhang and others made major three-dimensional contributions; these people are not on the supplied credit list, which leaves a real credit question.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed across materials and techniques, including angle-resolved photoemission on three-dimensional topological insulators. The 2016 prize recognised topological phase transitions, but this is a distinct development.
uncertainties: The missing names noted above create a risk that a three-person prize looks unfair.
The 2016 topological-phases prize may be seen as covering part of the conceptual territory.
Practical applications remain limited, though that is not a criterion for the discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of M87* and Sgr A* are direct visual evidence of black-hole shadows and test strong-field general relativity. I follow the gravity side of the field closely, and the achievement is remarkable. It is also an observation rather than a new principle, and the 2020 prize already recognised black holes in a different way.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed the shadow imaging idea, Doeleman led the very-long-baseline interferometry technique development, and Zensus was a key European leader of the programme. The Event Horizon Telescope is a collaboration of hundreds, so any three-person selection is a judgement and the allocation is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: M87* and Sgr A* have both been imaged and later polarisation results exist, so confirmation is good. Detailed interpretation, such as the spin and the accretion model, remains model-dependent, which makes the physics conclusions less settled than the image itself.
uncertainties: Model dependence of the inferred black-hole parameters.
Whether the committee views this as sufficiently distinct from the 2020 prize.
Fair allocation of credit within a very large collaboration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at magic angles and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created a new field, moire quantum matter. It is original and has had a very large influence on condensed matter physics.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the decisive 2011 prediction. Jarillo-Herrero's group made the 2018 experimental discovery. The theory-experiment pairing gives a clear and fair three-person configuration, though others, including Cao, Fatemi and Kim, contributed experimental steps; I cannot verify the fine detail.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups with rapid growth in the field, but the mechanism of the superconductivity is still debated and the full phase diagram is not settled. The field is young, so recognition may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: The origin of the superconducting state is unresolved.
The field is only about seven years past the experimental discovery.
Sample-dependence and twist-angle disorder complicate the interpretation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2008 discovery of superconductivity at 26 K in fluorine-doped LaFeAsO opened the iron-based high-temperature superconductors, the second family after the cuprates with transition temperatures above 50 K. It is a clear, specific materials discovery with large lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Hosono's group made the original discovery. The supplied credit lists a single name, which gives a simple attribution, though others achieved the rapid follow-on increases in transition temperature and the Kamihara paper is a joint group work I cannot parse from the supplied text.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced worldwide within months, with a large body of work; the pairing mechanism remains debated and no room-temperature application has emerged. Timing is reasonable after more than fifteen years.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism is not settled.
A single-laureate award for a group discovery may be seen as incomplete.
Hosono's earlier and separate work, for example on transparent oxide semiconductors, could complicate how the prize is framed.
